name: Biological Classification

questions.q: Which of the following character is common in Monera, Protista and Fungi?
questions.s: All three kingdoms contain organisms that possess a cell wall, although their composition varies (peptidoglycan in Monera, cellulosic/siliceous in some Protista, and chitin in Fungi).

questions.q: How many domain(s) in three domain system include prokaryotic organisms?
questions.s: In Carl Woese's three-domain system, two domains—Archaea and Bacteria—comprise prokaryotic organisms.

questions.q:
Match the Column-I with Column-II and select the correct option from code given below:

Column-I
A. Planaria
B. Fungi
C. Yeast
D. Amoeba

Column-II
(i) Binary fission
(ii) Budding
(iii) True regeneration
(iv) Fragmentation
questions.s: Planaria shows true regeneration, Fungi reproduce by fragmentation, Yeast by budding, and Amoeba by binary fission.

questions.q: Bacteria show a great diversity in:
questions.s: Though structurally very simple, bacteria exhibit extensive metabolic diversity.

questions.q: Kingdom Protista forms a link with:
questions.s: Kingdom Protista connects unicellular prokaryotes to the other three eukaryotic kingdoms: Plantae, Fungi, and Animalia.

questions.q: Members of Kingdom Protista are primarily:
questions.s: Members of Kingdom Protista are predominantly aquatic organisms.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct statement about Archaebacteria?
o: They differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure.
This cell wall structure is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.
Methanogens are present in the gut of several ruminant animals.
questions.s: Archaebacteria possess a distinct cell wall composition that enables them to inhabit extreme environments; methanogens occur in ruminant guts.

questions.q: Cyanobacteria are also known as:
questions.s: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes commonly referred to as blue-green algae.

questions.q: The colonies of cyanobacteria are generally surrounded by:
questions.s: Colonies of Cyanobacteria are typically enveloped by a gelatinous or mucilaginous sheath.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts?
questions.s: Nostoc and Anabaena are cyanobacteria that possess specialized thick-walled cells called heterocysts for nitrogen fixation.

questions.q: Mycoplasma are organisms that:
o: Are the smallest living cells known
questions.s: Mycoplasmas lack a cell wall, are the smallest known living cells, and are facultative anaerobes.

questions.q: Chief producers in the oceans are:
questions.s: Diatoms (a class of chrysophytes) are the chief primary producers in marine ecosystems.

questions.q: Diatomaceous earth is formed due to the deposition of cell walls of diatoms over billions of years. It is used in:
questions.s: Diatomaceous earth is gritty and porous, making it useful in polishing, filtration of oils, and syrups.

questions.q: Red tides in warm oceans are often caused by rapid multiplication of:
questions.s: Gonyaulax, a dinoflagellate, multiplies rapidly causing red tides.

questions.q: Instead of a cell wall, Euglenoids have a protein-rich layer called:
questions.s: Euglenoids lack a cell wall and instead have a flexible proteinaceous outer layer termed a pellicle.

questions.q: Under suitable conditions, slime moulds form an aggregation called:
questions.s: In favorable conditions, slime moulds aggregate to form a multinucleate mass called a plasmodium.

questions.q: During unfavorable conditions, slime moulds form:
questions.s: Under adverse conditions, the plasmodium differentiates into fruiting bodies bearing resistant spores.

questions.q: Which protozoan causes sleeping sickness?
questions.s: Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan parasite that causes sleeping sickness.

questions.q: Fungi show a great diversity in:
questions.s: Fungi display extensive diversity in both morphological form and environmental habitats.

questions.q: Cell wall of fungi is composed of:
questions.s: Fungal cell walls are predominantly composed of chitin and complex polysaccharides.

questions.q: Fungi prefer to grow in places that are:
questions.s: Warm and humid conditions favor fungal growth and spore germination.

questions.q: A network of hyphae in fungi is known as:
questions.s: The vegetative body of a fungus consists of a mass of thread-like hyphae known as a mycelium.

questions.q: Hyphae that are continuous tubes filled with multinucleated cytoplasm are called:
questions.s: Aseptate, multinucleate hyphae are termed coenocytic hyphae.

questions.q: Fungi storing food as:
questions.s: Fungi store reserve food material primarily in the form of glycogen and lipid/oil droplets.

questions.q: The sexual cycle in fungi involves three steps in which sequence?
questions.s: The fungal sexual cycle proceeds through Plasmogamy (fusion of protoplasm), Karyogamy (fusion of nuclei), and Meiosis.

questions.q: A dikaryon condition (n+n) is characteristic of:
questions.s: An intervening dikaryotic stage (n+n) occurs prominently in Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes.

questions.q: Members of Phycomycetes are found in:
o: Decaying wood in moist and damp places
questions.s: Phycomycetes inhabit aquatic habitats, decaying organic matter in damp areas, and act as obligate plant parasites.

questions.q: Asexual reproduction in Phycomycetes takes place by motile spores called _______ or non-motile spores called _______.
questions.s: In Phycomycetes, motile asexual spores are zoospores, whereas non-motile spores are aplanospores.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of Phycomycetes?
questions.s: Mucor, Rhizopus (bread mould), and Albugo (parasitic fungus on mustard) are all Phycomycetes.

questions.q: Ascomycetes are commonly known as:
questions.s: Ascomycetes are commonly called sac fungi because their sexual spores are produced inside a sac-like ascus.

questions.q: Which of the following is a unicellular ascomycete?
questions.s: Yeast (Saccharomyces) is a unicellular representative of Ascomycetes.

questions.q: Asexual spores in Ascomycetes are called _______ and are produced _______ on conidiophores.
questions.s: Ascomycetes produce asexual spores called conidia exogenously on specialized structures termed conidiophores.

questions.q: Sexual spores in Ascomycetes are called _______ and are produced _______ in sac-like asci.
questions.s: Ascospores are sexual spores generated endogenously within sac-like asci.

questions.q: Neurospora is extensively used in:
questions.s: Neurospora crassa is widely used as a model organism in experimental genetics and biochemistry.

questions.q: Morels and truffles belong to class _______ and are _______.
questions.s: Morels and truffles are edible members of Ascomycetes prized as delicacies.

questions.q: Commonly known forms of Basidiomycetes are:
questions.s: Basidiomycetes include mushrooms, bracket fungi, and puffballs.

questions.q: In Basidiomycetes, vegetative reproduction occurs commonly by:
questions.s: Vegetative propagation in Basidiomycetes proceeds predominantly through fragmentation.

questions.q: Sex organs are absent in which class of fungi, but sexual reproduction takes place by somatogamy?
questions.s: In Basidiomycetes, specialized sex organs are absent; sexual reproduction occurs by somatogamy between vegetative cells.

questions.q: Basidiospores are produced _______ on the basidium.
questions.s: Basidiospores are borne exogenously on the exterior of the basidium.

questions.q: Which of the following is a rust fungus belonging to Basidiomycetes?
questions.s: Puccinia causes rust diseases (e.g., wheat rust) and belongs to Basidiomycetes.

questions.q: Ustilago causes which disease in plants?
questions.s: Ustilago is commonly known as smut fungus and causes smut diseases in crops.

questions.q: Deuteromycetes are called 'imperfect fungi' because:
o: Only asexual or vegetative stages are known
questions.s: Deuteromycetes are termed imperfect fungi because their sexual (perfect) stage is absent or unknown.

questions.q: When sexual forms of Deuteromycetes were discovered, they were often moved to:
questions.s: Upon discovery of their perfect (sexual) stages, members of Deuteromycetes are reclassified into Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.

questions.q: Deuteromycetes reproduce only by asexual spores known as:
questions.s: Deuteromycetes reproduce asexually primarily through conidia.

questions.q: Which of the following belongs to Deuteromycetes?
questions.s: Alternaria, Colletotrichum, and Trichoderma are representative genera of Deuteromycetes.

questions.q: Bladderwort and Venus flytrap are examples of:
questions.s: Bladderwort and Venus flytrap are partially heterotrophic, insectivorous plants.

questions.q: Cuscuta is an example of a:
questions.s: Cuscuta (dodder) is a non-green parasitic plant.

questions.q: Plant cell walls are predominantly made of:
questions.s: The primary structural component of plant cell walls is cellulose.

questions.q: The life cycle of plants has two distinct phases - the diploid _______ and the haploid _______.
questions.s: Plants exhibit alternation of generations between a diploid sporophyte and a haploid gametophyte.

questions.q: Viruses did not find a place in Whittaker's classification system because:
questions.s: Whittaker's 5-kingdom system excluded viruses because they lack cellular organization and true living status outside a host.

questions.q: The name 'virus' (meaning venom or poisonous fluid) was given by:
questions.s: The term virus, meaning venom or poisonous fluid, was coined by Louis Pasteur (and recognized in early studies by Ivanowsky).

questions.q: Who demonstrated that the extract of infected tobacco plants could cause infection in healthy plants and called the fluid 'Contagium vivum fluidum'?
questions.s: M.W. Beijerinck (1898) coined 'Contagium vivum fluidum' (infectious living fluid) for tobacco mosaic pathogen.

questions.q: Who showed that viruses could be crystallized and crystals consist largely of proteins?
questions.s: W.M. Stanley (1935) crystallized Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) and showed it consists mostly of protein.

questions.q: In general, viruses that infect plants have _______ and viruses that infect animals have _______.
o: Single-stranded RNA; single or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA
questions.s: Plant viruses usually contain single-stranded RNA, whereas animal viruses possess ssRNA, dsRNA, or dsDNA.

questions.q: Bacteriophages (viruses that infect bacteria) usually have:
questions.s: Bacteriophages generally contain double-stranded DNA as their genetic material.

questions.q: The protein coat of a virus is called _______ and is made of small subunits called _______.
questions.s: The protective protein coat of a virus is the capsid, which consists of protein subunits called capsomeres.

questions.q: Viroids were discovered by:
questions.s: T.O. Diener discovered viroids in 1971 as infectious agents smaller than viruses.

questions.q: Viroids differ from viruses in that they:
o: Have free low molecular weight RNA
questions.s: Viroids lack a protein capsid, consist of naked low-molecular-weight RNA, and are smaller than viruses.

questions.q: Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by a:
questions.s: Potato spindle tuber disease (PSTD) is caused by a viroid.

questions.q: Prions are infectious agents consisting of abnormally folded:
questions.s: Prions are misfolded, infectious protein molecules devoid of nucleic acids.

questions.q: Which of the following diseases is caused by prions?
o: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) / Mad cow disease
questions.s: Prions cause BSE in cattle and its human variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD).

questions.q: Lichens are symbiotic associations between:
o: Fungi and roots of higher plants
questions.s: Lichens are mutualistic symbiotic associations between an algal component and a fungal component.

questions.q: In a lichen, the algal component is called _______ and the fungal component is called _______.
questions.s: The algal partner is the phycobiont (autotrophic) and the fungal partner is the mycobiont (heterotrophic).

questions.q: Lichens are very good indicators of:
questions.s: Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and serve as sensitive bioindicators of air pollution, especially SO2.

questions.q: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between:
o: Fungi and roots of higher plants
questions.s: Mycorrhiza represents a mutualistic association between fungi and roots of higher plants.

questions.q: The bacteria present in the gut of several ruminant animals
o: Are similar to other bacteria in cell wall structure
Are anaerobes with peptidoglycan cell wall
Are responsible for production of biogas
questions.s: Methanogenic archaebacteria in ruminant guts produce methane gas (biogas).

questions.q:
Find the incorrect statements from the following:
(I) Truffles - Club fungi
(II) Methanogens - Human intestine
(III) Thermoacidophiles - Hot sulphur springs
(IV) Slime moulds - True wall found in the vegetative stage.
(V) Whittaker's system of Classification brought together Chlamydomonas, Chlorella with Paramoecium, Amoeba in protista.
(VI) Roquefort cheese - Ascomycetes
questions.s: Truffles are sac fungi (Ascomycetes), methanogens inhabit ruminant guts, and slime mould spores (not vegetative stage) have true walls.

questions.q: Ciliates differ from all other protozoans in
o: having a contractile vacuole for removing excess water
questions.s: Ciliates display nuclear dimorphism, featuring a macronucleus for vegetative functions and a micronucleus for reproduction.

questions.q:
Study the following characters carefully and give answer:-
i. Bacterial structure is very simple because they are prokaryotic and unicellular
ii. Bacteria as a group show most extensive metabolic diversity
iii. Based on shape, bacteria are grouped into two categories only.
iv. Most of the bacteria do not have cell wall.
questions.s: Bacteria are simple prokaryotic single cells with vast metabolic diversity; they are grouped into four shapes and mostly have cell walls.

questions.q:
Select the correct answer
I. Chemosynthetic autotrophs bacteria oxidise various inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites and ammonia and use the released energy for their ATP production.
II. The organisms forming blooms in polluted water bodies are nutritionally Photosynthetic autotrophs.
questions.s: Chemosynthetic autotrophs derive energy from inorganic oxidations, and bloom-forming cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms in the list given below are autotrophs and perform oxygenic photosynthesis?
o: Anabaena, Sacharomyces, Green sulphur bacteria, Frankia
questions.s: Nostoc, Anabaena, and Oscillatoria are cyanobacteria that perform oxygenic photosynthesis.

questions.q:
Identify the organisms that produce their own food in kingdom Monera?
A. Algae
B. BGA
C. Cyanobacteria
D. Nitrifying bacteria
E. Mycoplasma
F. Nitrogen fixation bacteria
questions.s: BGA/Cyanobacteria (photoautotrophs) and nitrifying bacteria (chemoautotrophs) produce their own food in Monera.

questions.q: Kingdom Monera includes
o: Unicellular and multicellular microorganisms with simplest metabolism
The most ancient microorganisms which are nutritionally heterotrophs only
Most ancient, the smallest, and most abundant microorganisms
questions.s: Monera consists of unicellular prokaryotes, which are the most ancient, smallest, and abundant organisms.

questions.q: Identify the correct statement about three domains of life?
o: The three-domain system divides the Kingdom Monera into two domains
The three-domain system divides the Kingdom Monera into three domains
The three-domain system puts Kingdom Monera into first domain only
The three-domain system didnot include archaebacteria
questions.s: Carl Woese's three-domain system splits Kingdom Monera into Archaea and Bacteria.

questions.q: Sacharomyces, Albugo, Rhizopus, Ustilago, Puccinia, Agaricus, Trichoderma, Alternaria. Which of the following examples are belongs to class basidiomycetes.
questions.s: Ustilago (smut), Puccinia (rust), and Agaricus (mushroom) belong to Basidiomycetes.

questions.q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
(I) Plasmodium -> Slime moulds -> Saprotrophic protists
(II) Experimental genetic -> Neurospora -> Ascomycetes
(III) Prions -> PSTD -> Protein
(IV) Edible fungi -> Truffles and Morels -> Ascomycetes
(V) Animal virus -> ssRNA -> HIV
questions.s: Prions cause diseases like BSE/CJD (PSTD is a plant viroid disease), making statement III incorrect.

questions.q: Which of the following are found in extreme saline conditions?
questions.s: Halophilic Archaebacteria are specifically adapted to extreme saline conditions.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct statements?
o: Slime moulds are saprophytic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Mycoplasma have DNA, Ribosome and cell wall
Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
questions.s: Cyanobacteria are autotrophic photosynthetic monerans.

questions.q:
Select the correct answer about slimemould spores
i. The spores possess true walls.
ii. They are extremely resistant and survive for many years, even under adverse conditions
iii. The spores are dispersed by water currents
questions.s: Slime mould spores have true cell walls and high resistance; they are dispersed by air currents, not water.

questions.q: Protista is similar to Plantae and different from Monera in having:
o: Protista and Plantae have a nuclear membrane.
(II) Protista and Plantae are eukaryotes, whereas Monera are prokaryotes.
(III) All Protista and Plantae are chlorophyll bearing and perform photosynthesis.
(IV) Protista and Plantae have a cellulosic cell wall.
questions.s: Protists and Plants are eukaryotic organisms possessing nuclear membranes, unlike prokaryotic Monerans.

questions.q: Which statement is wrong for viruses?
o: They have ability to synthesise nucleic acids and proteins.
Antibiotics have no effect on them.
All of them have helical symmetry.
questions.s: Viruses exhibit various architectural forms including polyhedral, helical, and complex structures.

questions.q: Select the correct statement:-
o: Sporangiospores are exogenously produced in sporangium
In basidiomycetes asexual spores are generally not found.
Alternaria is a example of ascomycetes
questions.s: Asexual spores are generally absent in Basidiomycetes.

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are correct combinations with respect to their mycelium and mode of sexual reproduction:-
i. Albugo-Coenocytic mycelium and oogamy.
ii. Rhizopus- Aseptate mycelium and Isogamy.
iii. Puccinia - Septate mycelium and Anisogamy.
iv. Trichoderma - Aseptate mycelium and conidia formation
questions.s: Albugo and Rhizopus possess coenocytic/aseptate mycelia reproducing sexually via oogamy and isogamy respectively.

questions.q: Which one of the following also acts as a catalyst in a bacterial cell?
questions.s: 23S rRNA in the prokaryotic 50S ribosomal subunit acts as a ribozyme for peptidyl transferase activity.

questions.q: Which one of the following is true for fungi?
o: They lack a rigid cell wall
questions.s: Fungi are heterotrophic eukaryotes that absorb nutrients primarily as saprotrophs.

questions.q:
Which of the following are characteristics of members of Kingdom Protista?
i. Nucleus is present and DNA is associated with histone proteins.
ii. Cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S while organelle ribosomes are 70S.
iii. Members of the kingdom are heterotrophic with absorptive type of nutrition.
iv. Sap vacuoles are absent.
questions.s: Protists are eukaryotes with histone-associated DNA and possess 80S cytosolic and 70S organellar ribosomes.

questions.q:
Consider the statements
i. Organisms are known by only vegetative or asexual stage
ii. Most of the members are decomposers of litter
These statements are true for
questions.s: Deuteromycetes (Imperfect Fungi) are characterized by the absence of a known sexual stage and play a major role in decomposing litter.

questions.q:
What is the criteria used by Whittaker for classification?
(i) Cell structure (ii) Body organisation
(iii) Mode of nutrition (iv) Reproduction
(v) Phylogenetic relationship
(vi) Presence of mitochondria
(vii) Morphological character
o: i, ii, iii, iv, v, vi, vii
questions.s: Whittaker used five main criteria: cell structure, thallus organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

questions.q:
Identify the true (T) and false (F) statements w.r.t. diatoms
i. They are microscopic and float passively in water currents.
ii. Cell wall is made up of stiff cellulosic plates.
iii. Cell wall form two thin overlapping shells which fit together as in soap box.
iv. Cell wall is destructible and over few hundred years forms
o: i-F, ii-T, iii - T, iv - F
i-T, ii-T, iii - F, iv - F
questions.s: Diatoms float as plankton (i-T), have silica shells instead of cellulose (ii-F), fit like a soap box (iii-T), and possess non-destructible walls (iv-F).

questions.q: Nuclear membrane is absent in
questions.s: Nostoc is a prokaryotic cyanobacterium, so it lacks a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.q: Single celled eukaryotes are included in
questions.s: All single-celled eukaryotic organisms are categorized under Kingdom Protista.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about Ascomycetes. Which one of the statement given below is false?
o: They are saprophytic, decomposer, coprophilous and parasitic
Aspergillus, Claviceps, and Neurospora are important examples of Ascomycetes
questions.s: The mycelium in Ascomycetes is branched and septate, not coenocytic.

questions.q:
Match Column I with Column II
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. Rhizopus - P. Mushroom
B. Ustilago - Q. Smut fungus
C. Puccinia - R. Bread mould
D. Agaricus - S. Rust fungus
questions.s: Rhizopus is bread mould, Ustilago is smut fungus, Puccinia is rust fungus, and Agaricus is mushroom.

questions.q:
Character belongs to slime moulds
A. Saprophytes
B. Forms plasmodium under unfavourable condition
C. Spores posses true walls
D. Spores are dispersed by water
E. Body moves along decaying twings and leaves engulfing organic matter.
questions.s: Plasmodium forms under favorable conditions, and spores are dispersed by air currents, making B and D false.

questions.q: Select the correct statement..
o: Members of kingdom fungi show a great diversity in structures and habitat
Most fungi are saprophytic, some are parasites and some symbiotic
There are four classes under kingdom fungi
questions.s: Fungi display wide diversity in structure, habitat, nutrition, and are categorized into four major classes.

questions.q: In which group of organisms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells which fit together?
questions.s: In Chrysophytes (specifically diatoms), cell walls form two overlapping siliceous shells fitting together like a soap box.

questions.q: Pick up the wrong statement
o: Cell wall is absent in Animalia.
Protists have photosynthetic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition.
Nuclear membrane is present in Monera.
questions.s: Kingdom Monera contains prokaryotes, which lack an organized nuclear membrane.

questions.q: Which of the following statement about Euglena is/are true?
o: The pigments of Euglena are quite different from those of green plants
questions.s: Euglenoids bear flagella and are mixotrophic, behaving heterotrophically in the dark.

questions.q:
What is true regarding plasmids?
(I) Plasmids are used to monitor genetic transformation.
(II) Plasmids are present in bacterial cells.
(III) Plasmids are organisms with antibiotic resistance.
(IV) Plasmids are DNA molecules with Ori (origin of replication).
questions.s: Plasmids are extrachromosomal DNA molecules containing an Ori, found in bacteria, used in monitoring genetic transformation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option, stating which one is true (T) and which one is false (F)?
i. Blue green algae are the photosynthetic monerans.
ii. Genetic material in eukaryotes is circular, double stranded, helical DNA not enclosed by nuclear envelope
iii. Sexual reproduction in Rhizopus is oogamous and the mode of sexual fusion is gametangial contact type.
iv. Noctiluca is the first dinoflagellate to show bioluminescence.
v. The fungal component of lichen is called phycobiont and the algal component is called mycobiont.
o: i-T, ii-F, iii - F, iv-T, v - F
i-T, ii-F, iii - F, iv-T, v-T
i-T, ii-F, iii - T, iv - F, v-T
i-F, ii-F, iii - F, iv-T, v-F
questions.s: i is T; ii is F (eukaryotic DNA is linear and enclosed); iii is F (isogamous); iv is T; v is F (fungal component is mycobiont).

questions.q:
The unique kingdom of heterotrophic organisms with loose tissue level organisation shows
i. Diversity in habitat
ii. Diversity in morphology of mycelium
iii. Chitin in cell wall
iv. Degeneration of sex organs from lower to higher group
v. Optimum in growth in cool and humid places
o: i, ii, iii and v are correct
questions.s: Fungi grow best in warm and humid conditions, making statement v incorrect.

questions.q: Chrysophytes, Euglenoids, Dinoflagellates and Slimemoulds are included in the kingdom
questions.s: Chrysophytes, Euglenoids, Dinoflagellates, and Slime moulds are single-celled eukaryotic protists.

questions.q:
The following features belongs to class
A. Sexual spores produced endogenously.
B. Asexual spores conidia produced exogenously.
C. Many members of this class are edible.
questions.s: Ascomycetes produce exogenous conidia and endogenous ascospores, with several edible members like morels and truffles.

questions.q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
(I) Antibiotic source - Penicillium-Ascomycetes
(II) Paramecium - Ciliated protozoan - Two nuclei
(III) Trypanosoma - Flagellated protist - Sleeping sickness
(IV) Viroids - PSTD-DNA
(V) Yeast - Unicellular - Ascospore
questions.s: Viroids contain free RNA, not DNA; hence IV is incorrect while I, II, III, and V are correct matches.

questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement regarding Kingdon Monera.
o: Bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera.
They are the most abundant micro-organisms.
They also live in extreme habitats such as hot springs, deserts, snow and deep oceans where very few other life forms can survive.
Bacteria are categorized into 4 groups based on their nutrition.
questions.s: Bacteria are categorized into 4 groups based on shape (Coccus, Bacillus, Vibrium, Spirillum), not nutrition.

questions.q: Select the correct option w.r.t Archaebacteria.
questions.s: Halophiles inhabit extreme salty areas, Thermoacidophiles live in hot springs, and Methanogens occur in marshy areas and ruminant guts.

questions.q:
Read the following statements and select the correct option.
Statement A: Cyanobacteria are unicellular, colonial or filamentous, marine or terrestrial algae.
Statement B: The colonies are generally surrounded by gelatinous sheath.
o: Both statements A and B are correct.
Statement A is correct and statement B is incorrect.
Statement A is incorrect and statement B is correct.
Both statements A and B are incorrect.
questions.s: Cyanobacteria are unicellular, colonial or filamentous algae found in freshwater, marine or terrestrial habitats, enclosed in a gelatinous sheath.

questions.q: Organism which play a great role in recycling nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorous, iron and sulphur are
questions.s: Chemosynthetic autotrophs oxidize inorganic substances to release energy and recycle nitrogen, phosphorus, iron, and sulfur.

questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
o: Heterotrophic bacteria are most abundant in nature.
They are helpful in making curd from milk, production of antibiotics, fixing nitrogen in legume roots, etc.
Some are pathogens causing damage to human beings, crops, farm animals and pets. Cholera, typhoid, tetanus, citrus canker are well known diseases caused by different viruses.
questions.s: Cholera, typhoid, tetanus, and citrus canker are bacterial diseases, not viral.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding Mycoplasma?
o: Organisms that completely lack a cell wall.
Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants.
questions.s: Mycoplasmas lack cell walls, are the smallest known cells, survive anaerobically, and cause plant and animal diseases.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option.
Statement A: Chrysophytes are found in fresh water as well as in marine environments.
Statement B: Diatoms have cell walls forming two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box.
o: Both statements A and B are correct.
Statement A is correct and statement B is incorrect.
Statement A is incorrect and statement B is correct.
Both statements A and B are incorrect.
questions.s: Chrysophytes inhabit fresh and marine waters, and diatoms possess overlapping siliceous shells like a soap box.

questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding Euglenoids:
I. Majority of them are fresh water organisms found in stagnant water.
II. Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.
III. They have two flagella, a short and a long one.
IV. Though they are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight, when deprived of sunlight they behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms.
o: I, II and III are correct
I, II, III and IV are correct
questions.s: All given statements accurately describe euglenoid habitat, pellicle, flagellar setup, and mixotrophic nutrition.

questions.q: Spores of slime moulds possess
questions.s: Spores of slime moulds are resistant because they possess true cell walls.

questions.q:
Read the following statements and select the correct option.
Statement A: Protozoans are believed to be primitive relatives of animals.
Statement B: All protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites.
o: Both statements A and B are correct.
Statement A is correct and statement B is incorrect.
Statement A is incorrect and statement B is correct.
Both statements A and B are incorrect.
questions.s: Protozoans are heterotrophic eukaryotic protists regarded as primitive animal relatives.

questions.q:
Select the correct option representing the missing terms A, B, C and D in the given table:

Class | Asexual spores | Sexual spores | Mycelium
Phycomycetes | Zoospore / Aplanospore | Zygospore | Aseptate, Coenocytic

questions.q: Virus particle outside a living host cell is:
questions.s: Viruses exist as inert crystalline virions outside host cells.

questions.q: Infectious living fluid concept (Contagium vivum fluidum) was proposed by Beijerinck in:
questions.s: M.W. Beijerinck proposed Contagium vivum fluidum in 1898.

questions.q: W.M. Stanley crystallized Tobacco Mosaic Virus in:
questions.s: W.M. Stanley successfully crystallized TMV in 1935.

questions.q: Genetic material in viruses is:
questions.s: Viruses contain either DNA or RNA as genetic material, never both.

questions.q: Viruses that infect plants typically contain:
questions.s: Plant viruses predominantly carry single-stranded RNA genomes.

questions.q: Viruses that infect bacteria (bacteriophages) usually have:
questions.s: Bacteriophages typically possess double-stranded DNA genomes.

questions.q: Subunits of viral protein coat capsid are called:
questions.s: Capsids are assembled from individual protein subunits called capsomeres.

questions.q: Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by:
questions.s: PSTD is a classic plant disease caused by a viroid.

questions.q: Viroids differ from viruses because they lack:
questions.s: Viroids are naked RNA strands lacking any protective protein capsid.

questions.q: Prions consist of abnormally folded:
questions.s: Prions are misfolded, infectious proteinaceous agents.

questions.q: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) affects which farm animals?
questions.s: BSE (Mad Cow Disease) is a neurodegenerative disorder affecting cattle.

questions.q: In lichens, the autotrophic component is called _______ and heterotrophic component is called _______.
questions.s: Phycobiont (algae) is autotrophic; Mycobiont (fungus) is heterotrophic.

questions.q: Lichens serve as excellent bioindicators for:
questions.s: Lichens are sensitive to sulfur dioxide (SO_2) levels in ambient air.

q: A dikaryon is formed when
o: The two haploid cells do not fuse immediately
s: A dikaryon is an intervening stage (n + n) where two haploid cells undergo plasmogamy but their nuclei do not fuse immediately.

q: Which of the following statement about plant is false?
o: Plants show alternation of generations during their life cycle
s: Plants are non-motile (immotile) multicellular eukaryotic autotrophs.

q:
Select from the following the total number of features belonging to animal kingdom.
1. Multicellular, heterotrophic.
2. Most of them capable of locomotion.
3. Have definite shape and size.
4. Digestion of food in internal cavity.
5. Holozoic mode of nutrition.
6. Stored food reserve as glycogen or fat.
7. Higher forms shows sensory and neuromotor mechanism.
8. Some members are autotrophic.
9. Presence of cellulose cell wall..
10. Sexual reproduction generally by copulation of male and female followed by embryological development
s: Features 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 10 are characteristic features of the Kingdom Animalia.

q: How many of the given organisms are obligate parasites which take over the machinery of the host cell? TMV, Nostoc, Bacteriophage, HIV, Oscillatoria
s: TMV, Bacteriophage, and HIV are viruses, which are obligate intracellular parasites that hijack host cellular machinery.

q: Which of the following statements is wrong for viroids?
o: Their RNA is of high molecular weight.
s: Viroids contain free RNA of low molecular weight and lack a protein coat.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat.
Prions consist of abnormally folded proteins.
s: The infective constituent in viruses is the genetic material (DNA or RNA), not the protein coat.

q: Find out the correct statement.
o: In lichens, the algal component is called phycobiont and fungal component is known as mycobiont, which are heterotrophic and autotrophic respectively.
Viroid contains RNA of low molecular weight and protein coat
A virus contains both RNA and DNA
s: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites that cannot replicate outside a host cell.

q:
Find the correct statements from the following:
(I) According to the five-kingdom classification of R.H. Whittaker, producers are placed in Monera, Protista, and Plantae,
(II) In Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, eukaryotes are assigned to all five kingdoms.
(III) Saccharomyces is unicellular and useful in fermentation.
(IV) According to the three-domain theory, two domains include prokaryotic organisms.
(V) Euglenoids have two flagella, one lies longitudinally and the other transversely.
(VI) Slime mould spores are dispersed by air currents.
s: Statements I, III, IV, and VI are correct; eukaryotes are in four kingdoms, and dinoflagellates (not euglenoids) have longitudinal and transverse flagella.

q:
Consider the organisms mentioned and select the number of heterotrophs
Green sulphur bacteria, Purple sulphur bacteria, Iron bacteria, Sulphur bacteria, Frankia, Nostoc, Rhizobium, Vibrio
s: Frankia, Rhizobium, and Vibrio are heterotrophic organisms.

q: Which pair of the following belongs to Basidiomycetes?
s: Bird's nest fungi (Cyathus) and puffballs (Lycoperdon) belong to the class Basidiomycetes.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Fusion of two cells is called Karyogamy.
Fusion of protoplasms between two motile on non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy.
Organisms that depend on living plants are called saprophytes.
Some of the organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called sheath cells.
s: Plasmogamy is defined as the fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes.

q:
Match the following classes of Fungi (Column-I) with the examples (Column-II).
Choose the correct option:
A. Phycomycetes
B. Ascomycetes
C. Basidiomycetes
D. Deuteromycetes

P. Penicillium
Q. Alternaria
R. Albugo
S. Puccinia
s: Albugo is a Phycomycete, Penicillium is an Ascomycete, Puccinia is a Basidiomycete, and Alternaria is a Deuteromycete.

q:
How many statements are correct for truffles and morels?
i. They have septate monokaryotic mycelium
ii. Reproduce asexually by nonmotile endogenous spores
iii. Produce haploid exogenous sexual spores arranged in an orderly manner
iv. Their fruiting bodies are edible
s: Morels and truffles are edible Ascomycetes; they produce endogenous ascospores in asci within ascocarps, making statements regarding edibility and orderly spore arrangement correct.

q: An association between roots of higher plants and fungi is called
s: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between a fungus and the roots of higher plants.

q:
Difference between virus and viroid is
(I) Absence of protein coat in viroid but present in virus.
(II) Presence of low molecular weight RNA in virus but absent in viroid.
(III) Some viruses have RNA as genetic material and viroids also have RNA as their genetic material.
s: Viroids lack a protein coat and possess low molecular weight RNA, unlike viruses which possess a protein coat.

q:
What is common in Ustilago, Neurospora, and Agaricus?
(I) All have a dikaryotic phase in their life cycle.
(II) All produce motile sexual spores.
(III) All are edible.
(IV) The mycelium is branched and septate.
s: Ustilago, Neurospora, and Agaricus all exhibit a dikaryotic phase (n+n) and have branched, septate mycelium.

q:
Consider the following statements about slime moulds.
I. Slime moulds are saprophytic protists
II. The spores possess true walls
Which of the statements(s) given above is/are correct?
o: I is true, But II is false
Both I and II are false
I is false but II is true
Both I and II are true
s: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists whose spores possess extremely resistant true walls.

q: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by
s: R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification in 1969.

q:
The following features represent which group of organisms?
(I) Microscopic
(II) Chief producers in oceans
(III) Found in fresh water as well as in marine environments, planktons.
(IV) Indestructible cell wall
(V) The walls are embedded with silica, making them indestructible.
s: Diatoms are microscopic, photosynthetic ocean producers with silica-embedded indestructible cell walls.

q: Curing of tea leaves is brought about by the activity of
s: Tea leaf curing is achieved through the enzymatic action of bacteria such as Micrococcus candidans.

q: Which of the following are likely to be present in deep sea water?
s: Archaebacteria are capable of surviving extreme habitats including deep ocean hydro-thermal vents.

q: Slime moulds - Under P conditions, they form an R called Q which may grow and spread over several feet. During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. In the above mentioned incomplete statement, labeling represents
o: P-Aggregation, Q- Plasmodium, R - Suitable condition
s: Under suitable conditions (P), slime moulds form an aggregation (R) called Plasmodium (Q).

q:
State whether the given statements are true or false.
I. Bacteria are simple in structure, but complex in behaviour
II. Some of the bacteria are autotrophic. They may be photosynthetic autotrophic or chemosynthetic autotrophic.
III. Heterotrophic nutrition involves obtaining nutrition either through parasitism or saprotrophism
o: I is true, II and II are false
I, II and III are true
s: Bacteria exhibit simple cellular structure with diverse metabolic strategies, including autotrophy and heterotrophy.

q:
The following characteristics are of which of the given fungi?
A. Sex organs are absent but plasmogamy is by fusion of two somatic cells of different strains or genotype.
B. Asexual spores are generally not found.
s: Basidiomycetes lack distinct sex organs and asexual spores; plasmogamy occurs via somatogamy.

q: Read the following statements and select the incorrect statement.
o: The cyanobacteria is an autrophic bacteria
The cyanobacteria are unicellular, colonial or filamentous, freshwater/ marine or terrestrial algae.
Mucor belongs to class phycomycetes of kingdom fungi
s: Bacteria exhibit diverse modes of nutrition, including autotrophic, parasitic, and saprophytic forms.

q:
Study the following statements and identify the correct option given below.
I. Viruses that infect plants have single-stranded RNA and viruses that infect animals have either single or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA
II. Bacterial viruses or Bacteriophages are usually single-stranded RNA viruses.
o: I is true, but II is false
I is false, but II is true
s: Plant viruses generally have ssRNA, whereas bacteriophages typically possess double-stranded DNA.

q: Choose the correct statement.
o: The cell wall is present in all monerans
The cell wall is present in all protistans
The cell wall is present in all the members of Plantae
s: All members of Kingdom Plantae possess cell walls composed primarily of cellulose.

q: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy is a disease caused by prions in a:
s: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow disease, affects cattle.

q: Choose the incorrect statement about members of kingdom-monera
o: All of them live in or on other organisms as parasites
Some synthesise their own food from inorganic solutes
Bacterial structure is very simple, they are very complex in behaviour.
Hundreds of bacteria are present in handful of soil
s: Monerans exhibit vast metabolic diversity; not all are parasitic, many are free-living autotrophs or saprophytes.

q: Archaebacteria differ from eubacteria in:
s: Archaebacteria possess a unique cell wall structure lacking peptidoglycan, enabling them to survive extreme conditions.

q: Association between Mycobiont and Phycobiont are found in
s: Lichens represent a symbiotic association between a fungal partner (mycobiont) and an algal partner (phycobiont).

q: A student while extracting DNA from Aspergillus fungus requires break open the cell wall. Name the enzyme used for the process?
s: Aspergillus is a fungus whose cell wall is rich in chitin; thus, chitinase is used to degrade its cell wall.

q: True nucleus is absent in:
s: Anabaena is a cyanobacterium (Moneran) and being a prokaryote, it lacks a true nucleus.

q: Some hypothermophilic organisms that grow in highly acidic (pH 2) habitats belong to the 2 groups
s: Thermoacidophiles belong to Archaea, while certain extremophilic Eubacteria also survive high temperature and low pH environments.

q: Which of the following shows coiled RNA strand and capsomeres?
s: Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) has a single-stranded helical RNA genome surrounded by helically arranged capsomeres.

q:
The following features belong to class
A. Members are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants
B. Fusion of gametes may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
C. Mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic.
D. Spores are endogenously produced in sporangium.
E. Asexual reproduction by zoospores or aplanospores.
s: Aseptate coenocytic mycelium and endogenous sporangiospores are characteristic of Phycomycetes.

q: Study the given properties. Which one option has all the properties found in all organisms of the five-kingdom classification?
s: All living organisms across the five kingdoms share a cellular plasma membrane and carry out cellular respiration.

q: Which among the following is not a prokaryote?
s: Saccharomyces (Yeast) is a unicellular eukaryotic fungus.

q: Select the wrong statement
o: W.M. Stanley showed that viruses could be crystallised.
The viroids were discovered by D.J. Ivanowsky.
Mosaic disease in tobacco and AIDS in human being are caused by viruses.
The term 'contagium vivum fluidum' was coined by Beijerinck.
s: Viroids were discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971, not by Ivanowsky.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

N₂ fixing bacteria pick up free N₂ from soil atmosphere and convert it into nitrogenous compounds.
Pathogenic bacteria cause 90% of human diseases
s: Mycoplasmas are facultative anaerobes and can survive in the complete absence of oxygen.

q: Which of the following components provide sticky character to the bacterial cell ?
s: Glycocalyx forms a capsule or slime layer giving a sticky consistency that helps in adhesion and protection.

q:

Claviceps.

s: Linnaeus proposed Two-Kingdom classification (Plantae and Animalia), and Mycoplasma is the smallest cell.

q: The motile bacteria are able to move by
s: Motile bacteria possess flagella composed of flagellin protein for locomotion.

q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
Plant virus - ssRNA - Mosaic disease
Zoospore - Asexual spore - Phycomycetes
Plasmodium - Sporozoan - Malaria
Rust fungi - Puccinia - Basidiomycetes
Conidia - Sexual spore - Ascospore
s: Conidia are asexual spores, making statement V incorrect while I, II, III, and IV are correct matches.

q:
How many statements/features are correct for bacteriophage?
i. They have polygonal head and envelope
ii. Contractile tail sheath present
iii. Tail fibres are absent
iv. Nucleic acid as double stranded circular DNA usually
s: Bacteriophages usually contain linear double-stranded DNA as their genetic material.

q: A bacterium is capable of withstanding extreme heat, dryness and toxic chemicals. This indicates that it is probably able to form:
s: Endospores are highly resistant resting structures formed inside certain bacteria like Bacillus and Clostridium.

q: Which one of the following organism is not an eukaryote?
s: Escherichia coli is a bacterium belonging to kingdom Monera and is therefore a prokaryote.

q:
Which of the following is true regarding Mycoplasma?
(I) They do not have a cell wall.
(II) They produce a cell wall made up peptidoglycan,
(III) They can survive without oxygen.
(IV) They can cause diseases in animals and plants.
s: Mycoplasmas lack a cell wall, can survive anaerobically, and cause pathogenic infections in plants and animals.

q:
How many organisms in the list given below are autotrophs?
Mucor, Albugo, Penicillium, Lactobacillus, Nostoc, Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, Streptomyces, Saccharomyces, Trypanosoma, Porphyra
s: Nostoc, Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, and Porphyra are autotrophic organisms.

q: Cell wall is absent in
s: Mycoplasmas are prokaryotes that completely lack a cell wall.

q: Which of the statements given below is incorrect?
o: Biological classification is the scientific ordering of organisms in a hierarchial series of groups on the basis of their relationships, i.e. morphological, evolutionary and other
Whittaker classified organisms on the basis of autotrophic and heterotrophic mode of nutrition
In five kingdom system of classification, living organisms can be divided into prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells on the basis of cell structure
Mycoplasma is the smallest acellular living organism
s: Mycoplasma is a cellular living organism, not acellular.

q:
Among the following how many of them belong to Phycomycetes.
I. Mucor
II. Albugo
III. Claviceps
IV. Agaricus
V. Puffballs
s: Mucor, Albugo, and Rhizopus belong to Phycomycetes.

q: Identify the algae known for a biological activity called bioluminescence.
s: Noctiluca is a dinoflagellate renowned for emitting light (bioluminescence).

q:
Read the following statement
(a) Monera reproduce only sexually
(b) Cyanobacteria are oxygenic
(c) Monerans have a true nucleus
(d) Monerans include unicellular eukaryotic organism
Choose the correct option:
s: Monerans reproduce primarily asexually, lack a true nucleus, and are unicellular prokaryotes.

q: Five kingdom system of classification suggested by R.H. Whittaker is not based on
o: Presence or absence of a well defined nucleus
s: Whittaker's criteria included cell structure, thallus organization, nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

q: Why are archaebacteria able to survive in extreme environments unlike other bacteria:
o: They are heterotrophic and depend on decaying organic matter.
They produce large amounts of biogas which helps them survive.
Their cell wall structure is fundamentally different, enabling adaptation to harsh conditions.
They undergo photosynthesis at very high temperatures
s: Archaebacteria possess a distinctive cell wall composition that enables them to endure harsh, extreme conditions.

q: Select the wrong statement :-
o: Bacterial cell wall is made up of peptidoglycan.
Pilli and fimbriae are mainly involved in motility of bacterial cells.
s: Pili and fimbriae function in surface attachment and conjugation, not cell motility.

q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
(I) Bread mould - Ascomycetes
(II) Oospore - Sexual spore
(III) Chief oceanic producers - Diatoms
(IV) Red tide- Dinoflagellates
(V) Mixotrophic nutrition - Euglenoids
s: Bread mould (Rhizopus) belongs to Phycomycetes, making statement I incorrect.

q:
Read the following pair:-
i. Diatoms-haploid body
ii. Dinoflagellates-water bloom
iii. Slime moulds-decomposer nature
iv. Euglenoids-some time behave like predator
v. Protozoa-Unicellular prokaryotes
Choose the correct option :-
s: Diatoms have a diploid body, and protozoans are unicellular eukaryotes.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Morels and truffles are edible delicacies.
Claviceps is a source of many alkaloids and LSD.
Conidia are produced exogenously and ascospores endogenously.
Yeasts have filamentous bodies with long thread-like hyphae.
s: Yeast is a unicellular non-filamentous fungus and lacks hyphae.

q:
Which of the following are the characters of dinoflagellates?
(i) They are planktonic golden yellow algae with soap box like structure.
(ii) They are marine red biflagellated protists.
(iii) They appear yellow, green, brown, blue and red in colour.
(iv) They are biflagellated organisms with pellicle.
(v) They are saprophytic (or) parasitic unicellular forms.
s: Dinoflagellates are marine photosynthetic protists showing diverse pigmentation and two flagella.

q: Euglena, Nostoc, Chlorella, Mangifera Select the correct statement with respect to all these organisms:
o: All are photosynthetic and act as producers in nature.
Presence of chloroplast and cell wall.
s: All four organisms listed perform photosynthesis and function as primary producers.

q: Virus envelope is known as
s: The protein coat enclosing viral nucleic acid is called the capsid.

q:
Study the following statements and identify the correct ones:
(I) Diatoms float passively in water currents.
(II) Red tides are formed due to bioluminescence.
(III) Dinoflagellates are mostly fresh water organisms and photosynthetic.
(IV) Chrysophytes are found in freshwater as well as in marine environments.
s: Diatoms float passively as plankton, and Chrysophytes occur in both marine and fresh waters.

q:
Match the following in relation to fungi.
A. Penicillium
B. Yeast
C. Puccinia
D. Trichoderma

P. Sexual reproduction absent
Q. Wheat rust fungus
R. Exogenous asexual spores and endogenous sexual spores
S. Budding
s: Penicillium forms exogenous conidia/endogenous ascospores; Yeast reproduces by budding; Puccinia causes wheat rust; Trichoderma lacks sexual reproduction.

q: Which of the following does not apply to ascomycetes?
o: Asexual spores called conidia are produced endogenously
s: Ascomycetes have septate mycelium, are called sac fungi, and produce conidia exogenously.

q:
Select the incorrect statement with respect to dinoflagellates:
(I) These are golden-brown photosynthetic protists.
(II) They are mostly marine, and some are found in fresh water.
(III) They appear yellow, green, brown, blue, or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells.
(IV) Most of them are filamentous and lack flagella except in the reproductive stage.
s: Dinoflagellates are unicellular protists that characteristically possess two flagella.

q: The Cyanobacteria are also referred to as
s: Cyanobacteria are commonly known as blue-green algae due to phycocyanin and chlorophyll pigments.

q: Slime moulds and Unicellular algae are included in the kingdom protista because
o: Kingdom Protista includes eukaryotic organisms that do not clearly belong in the other three kingdoms
They lack important characteristics of the fungi and plants
They appear to be more closely related to unicellular eukaryotes
s: Kingdom Protista serves as a broad category encompassing diverse single-celled eukaryotic organisms.

q: The most abundant prokaryotes helpful to humans in making curd from milk and in production of antibiotics are the ones categorized as
s: Heterotrophic bacteria like Lactobacillus are used in curd generation and antibiotic synthesis.

q: Which of the following statements is/are incorrect?
o: Under unfavourable conditions, bacteria produce spores
Bacteria reproduce by a sort of asexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of RNA transfer from one bacterium to other
s: Bacteria multiply mainly by binary fission and achieve genetic recombination by primitive DNA transfer.

q: Viruses are non-cellular organisms but replicate themselves once they infect the host cell. To which of the following kingdom do viruses belong to?
s: Viruses are non-cellular entities and are not assigned to any of Whittaker's five kingdoms.

q: Difference between Virus and Viroid is
o: Absence of protein coat in viroid but present in virus
Presence of low molecular weight RNA in virus but absent in viroid
s: Viroids are infectious naked RNA molecules that lack the protein capsid found in viruses.

q: Why is a capsule advantageous to a bacterium?
o: It allows the bacterium to attach to the surface
It protects the bacterium from desiccation
It allows bacterium to hide from hosts immune system
s: The capsule protects pathogenic bacteria from phagocytosis by the host's immune defense system.

q: Which one single organism or pair of organism is correctly assigned to its or their taxonomic group?
o: Yeast used in making bread and beer in fungus
Nostoc and Anabaena are examples of protista
Lichen is a composite organism formed from the symbiotic association of an algae and a protozoan..
Paramecium and Plasmodium belong to the same kingdom as that of Penicillium.
s: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Yeast) is a unicellular fungus used extensively in baking and brewing.

q: Which of the statement(s) given below is/are correct?
o: Kingdom-Protista forms a link between monerans and the other organisms like plants, animal and fungi
Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by a process involving cell fusion and zygote formation
Being prokaryotic, the protistan cell body contains a well-defined nucleus and other membrane bound organelles
s: Protists are eukaryotic organisms that connect prokaryotic monerans with multicellular kingdoms.

q:
(I) Cholera
(II) Tetanus
(III) Plague
(IV) Turnip mosaic
(V) Citrus canker
(VI) Polio
Which of the following diseases mentioned above are caused by bacteria?
s: Cholera, tetanus, plague, and citrus canker are bacterial infections.

q:
The following fungus belongs to class ascomycetes (count the total number).
Rhizopus, Penicillium, Neurospora, Yeast, Mucor, Agaricus, Toadstool, Albugo, Claviceps, Alternaria, Trichoderma, Aspergillus, Ustilago, Morels, Truffles, Colletotrichum, Puccinia
s: Penicillium, Neurospora, Yeast, Claviceps, Aspergillus, Morels, and Truffles (7 total) belong to Ascomycetes.

q: What is the role of heterocysts in a cyanobacterial filament?
o: They carry out photosynthesis and nitrogen fixation.
They oxidize inorganic substances to obtain energy.
They carry out only nitrogen fixation.
s: Heterocysts are specialized cells that maintain anaerobic conditions exclusively to fix atmospheric nitrogen.

q:
Which of the following environmental conditions are essential for optimum growth of Mucor on a piece of bread?
A) Temperature of about 25°C
B) Temperature of about 5°C
C) Relative humidity of about 5%
D) Relative humidity of about 95%
E) A shady place
F) A brightly illuminated place
Choose the answer from the following options?
s: Mucor thrives best in warm (~25°C), moist (~95% RH), and shaded places.

q: Pigment-containing membranous extensions in some cyanobacteria are
s: Chromatophores are internal membrane extensions in photosynthetic prokaryotes containing pigments.

q: When a fresh water protozoan is placed in marine water:
o: The contractile vacuole increases in size
A number of contractile vacuoles appear
s: In hypertonic seawater, osmoregulation is unnecessary to expel excess water, so contractile vacuoles disappear.

q: Consider the following statements, Which of the statements given below is incorrect?
o: All prokaryotic organisms were grouped together under kingdom-Archae
The unicellular eukaryotic organisms were placed in kingdom-Protista
Chlorella and Chlamydomonas, are placed in protista in 5- kingdom classification
Paramecium and Amoeba lack cell walls
s: Prokaryotic organisms were grouped together under Kingdom Monera, not Archaea.

q: Black (stem) rust of wheat is caused by:
s: Black stem rust of wheat is caused by the fungal pathogen Puccinia graminis.

q: Thermococcus, Methanococcus, and Methanobacterium exemplify
o: Archaebacteria that contain protein homologous to eukaryotic core histones
Archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is negatively supercoiled
Bacteria that contain a cytoskeleton and ribosomes
Bacteria whose DNA relaxed or positively supercoiled but which have al cytoskeleton as well as mitochondria
s: These organisms are Archaebacteria that possess histone-like proteins homologous to eukaryotic histones.

q: Which is incorrect about phycomycetes?
o: A zygospore is formed by fusion of gametes
Asexual reproduction takes place by motile zoospores and non-motile aplanospores
White spots seen on mustard leaves are due to parasitic fungus Rhizopus
s: White spots on mustard leaves are caused by Albugo candida, not Rhizopus.

q: Select the wrong statement:
o: Pseudopodia are locomotory and feeding structures in Sporozoans
Cell wall is present in members of Fungi and Plantae
Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell in all kingdoms except Monera
s: Sporozoans lack specialized locomotory structures like pseudopodia; pseudopodia are found in amoeboids.

q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect?
o: Protistan body includes a well-defined nucleus, and no cellular organelles
Protists have nucleus along with flagella and cilia which doesnot confer motility
Protist cells have no nucleus but have some cellular organelles to perform basic functions
s: Protists are unicellular eukaryotes possessing a true nucleus, membrane-bound organelles, and motile cilia/flagella.

q:
Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization.
A. Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin.
B. Heterotrophs with tissue/organ/organ system level of body organization.
C. Prokaryotes with cell wall made of polysaccharides and amino acids.
D. Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/organ level of body organization.
E. Eukaryotes with cellular body organization.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
s: The increasing structural complexity sequence is Monera (C) -> Protista (E) -> Fungi (A) -> Plantae (D) -> Animalia (B).

q: After karyogamy followed by meiosis, spores are produced exogenously in
s: Agaricus is a Basidiomycete, producing basidiospores exogenously on the basidium.

q: What is incorrect for chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria :-
o: Oxidise various organic and inorganic substances
Uses the energy released through oxidation for their ATP production
Play great role in recycling of nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur
